question: Which of the following is NOT a writ issued by the Supreme Court of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jus soli**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jus soli** is a term that refers to the right of anyone born in the territory of a state to nationality or citizenship, which is not a writ issued by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The writs issued by the Supreme Court of India include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari**.
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is used to **secure the release of a person who has been unlawfully detained**.
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a** higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction**.
 
• The writ of **Quo Warranto** is used to **challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The writ of **Mandamus** is issued by the court to **compel a public authority to perform its duty**.
 
• The writ of **Certiorari** is issued by a** higher court to a lower court to transfer a case for review**.
 
• These writs are a part of the judicial review mechanism in India to ensure the protection of fundamental rights.
 
• The power to issue these writs is vested in the Supreme Court under **Article 32** and in the High Courts under **Article 226** of the Constitution of India.
 
• These writs are essential tools to maintain the rule of law and to ensure that public authorities act within their legal bounds.
